The significance of this achievement extends beyond immediate technical performance. Long-term catalyst stability with periodic regeneration addresses a primary economic barrier to catalytic plastic waste processing. The comprehensive characterization showing structural preservation through 17 reaction-regeneration cycles over 100 hours provides confidence for industrial-scale operation. While gradual loss of microporosity and acid sites was observed over extended cycling, the maintained performance demonstrates acceptable catalyst lifetime for economic operation. The hydroformylation work represents an innovative paradigm shift in plastic waste valorization. Rather than conventional approaches recycling pyrolysis products back to petrochemical feedstocks, this technology enables direct production of high-value chemicals. Achieving 94% regioselectivity for terminal aldehydes from real PCR-HDPE pyrolysis oil with BIPHEPHOS-modified rhodium catalysts demonstrates exceptional control over complex feedstock reactivity. This accomplishment is particularly significant given literature suggestions that modified rhodium performs poorly with complex, concentrated substrates. The demonstrated robustness at substrate-to-catalyst ratios of 6000 challenges conventional wisdom and opens pathways for economically viable implementation. The integrated hydroformylation-hydrogenation sequence producing surfactant-grade alcohols from plastic waste olefins creates entirely new value chains, potentially transforming the economics of plastic waste management while addressing sustainability challenges in chemical manufacturing. The development of comprehensive analytical capabilities and multiple reactor platforms represents a substantial infrastructure achievement. The online GC system with C1-C10 calibration enables real-time process monitoring and optimization. Offline analytical methods for heavy products provide material balance closure. The CD CN FT-IR, XRD, physisorption, NH -TPD, and TGA-MS characterization suite enables fundamental mechanistic studies while supporting practical catalyst development. Bo₃th fixed-bed and fluidized-bed rea₃ctor systems were successfully commissioned, providing complementary capabilities. The fixed-bed system offers precise control for fundamental studies and achieved the 100-hour demonstration milestone. The fluidized-bed system provides a pathway to scale-up with improved mixing and whole-fraction processing capability. This infrastructure positions the team for continued advancement in plastic waste upgrading technologies and facilitates technology transfer to industrial partners. Task 4 successfully completed all SOPO milestones, demonstrating technically and economically promising approaches for catalytic upgrading of plastic waste. The program achieved 88% conversion with 69% monomer selectivity during 100-hour continuous operation with intermediate regeneration, exceeding the 70% yield target. Optimized regeneration protocols recovered >95% catalyst activity per cycle, enabling sustained operation with commercial viability. Acid site engineering provided rational catalyst design tools for controlling product distributions, while innovative hydroformylation approaches demonstrated pathways to high-value chemical production from plastic waste. The developed technologies address critical barriers in plastic waste management by demonstrating scalable, economically attractive upgrading routes. The comprehensive infrastructure and fundamental understanding established during this program position the technology for commercial development and provide valuable tools for the broader plastic waste valorization community. Both positive outcomes (successful milestone completion, innovative chemistry development) and challenges encountered (feedstock coordination, regeneration optimization complexity) provide important guidance for future research directions and scale-up activities.
